newsitem.title: USA: AirTouch says could exceed cash flow goal.
newsitem.headline: AirTouch says could exceed cash flow goal.

text.p: AirTouch Communications said Wednesday it expects proportionate operating cash flow to approach $1 billion for the year 1996, and in light of the company's third quarter performance that goal could be exceeded.
AirTouch also said in a statement its expects to add at least 1.2 million cellular customers worldwide during 1996.
Losses from the continued construction and build-out of start-up operations in Italy, Poland, Spain, South Korea and India are expected to be about $130 million during 1996, it said.
The company had previously expected start-up losses of $100 million and attributed the higher loss to stronger than projected subscriber growth and ownership increases.

As the company continues to expand its operations domestically and internationally, capital requirements are expected to reach about $1 billion in 1996, excluding the recent $1.65 billion merger with Cellular Communications Inc.

AirTouch said that because of successful cost containment efforts and growing customer base, third quarter proportionate operating cash flow (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) increased 97 percent over the prior year to $327.5 million.
Because of the nature of the capital-intensive, high-growth industry, this is a very important measure of its financial performance, AirTouch said.
